families.name: shared-prefix
families.why: Every candidate is the same prefix value followed by its own tail, so the merged source computes the prefix once and duplicates the value with `dup`: extraction emits one node per shared value. This family is where a content-sharing saving is possible at all.
families.prefix: dup dup dup * * swap 5 * + dup * 3 - dup 7 * + 11 + dup dup * 13 - +

families.name: distinct-prefix
families.why: Every candidate is an independent program over the one input, with no value common to two candidates beyond the input node itself. Merging cannot remove work here, so the two merged arms are the same program: their difference measures the host's timing noise floor.

vectors.prng: splitmix64 on the seed, each draw folded to its absolute value modulo (range + 1)

arms.name: merged
arms.programs: one multi-output graph holding every candidate

arms.name: merged-duplicated
arms.programs: the same candidates with every reuse of the shared value replaced by a recomputation

arms.name: floor
arms.programs: the merged graph over one row

timing.order: arms are run in the frozen order rotated by the round index, so no arm always runs first
timing.cold: the warmup round is reported as `first`; this host cannot drop page caches without root, so `first` only means `not previously executed by this run`

decisions.d1: on `shared-prefix`, the merged arm's warm median wall time is at most 0.75x the separate arm's, i.e. evaluating one merged graph saves at least a quarter of the family's end-to-end evaluation time
decisions.d2: on `shared-prefix`, the merged arm is at most 0.90x the merged-duplicated arm, i.e. sharing one value is measurably cheaper than recomputing it inside one process
decisions.d3: on `distinct-prefix` the two merged arms are the same program, so their relative difference must stay inside the declared noise band; a larger difference invalidates the measurement instead of supporting d2
decisions.d4: every arm's peak resident set in its second warm round exceeds its first warm round by at most the declared bound
decisions.go: GO for further merged-execution work needs every correctness gate, d1, d2, d3 and d4. d1 without d2 records process amortisation only and is not a common-subexpression-elimination result. No outcome licenses an optimal-runtime claim.

not_measured: net arm: no interaction-net entry point exists in `crates/`; pending #37
labelled-SUP arm: no labelled DUP/SUP contract exists; pending #105
allocation counts: the workspace forbids `unsafe`, so no counting allocator can exist; only process peak RSS is reported
interaction counts: only the net reducer would report them; the graph evaluator reports nodes, layers and extraction counters instead
in-process CSE: the graph evaluator has no memoising pass, so a `merged` arm that repeats a subterm pays for it twice — this lane shares by construction and measures the difference
